## Review: not ready

From `/review-work`, which checks this PR against #199's Done-when and the repo's rules. It doesn't look for bugs; `/code-review` does that.

**Checks:** 9 pass, 0 fail, 0 pending (`landed-identity` skips until merge). Audit: one commit; `## Plan`, `## Test plan` and `Closes #199`; no generated artifacts.

**Done when:** each item is backed by the Test plan or the diff. `sync-resolves-network-addressing-from-one-source.sh` passed 31 checks, covering each rejection case. The `seed-route-renders-*` regression scripts pass with `CONFIG_REPO_PRIVATE=true`.

### Gap

The new §28 History entry in `docs/Decisions.md` (2026-11-04, #199) cites "the operator's answers on #199" as its reason for one change: "all of the addressing fields" now means "a `cidr`". None of #199's comments says that. At the base, §28 says a git `kind: Network` "carries either all of the addressing fields or none of them".

The Plan names this reading and explains it: a strict reading would break "today's fleets sync unchanged", since some fleets have no `dns` or no range. It still changes a binding rule, so it needs the operator's sign-off. After sign-off, reword the History line so it gives the real reason. The alternative is to keep the base rule.

### Decisions

§12 follows · §27 follows · §28 departs (the Plan names it; see the gap) · §29 follows · §31 not applicable

### Landing order with #518

Nothing to do yet. This PR and #518 conflict in `cmd/web/main.go` and `docs/Config Schema.md`. As #199 expected, whichever lands second moves `CONFIG_REPO_PRIVATE` and `NETWORK_ADDRESSING_PATH` into `deployconfig.Settings` and `docs/Deployment.md`. If #518 lands first, its `TestReadsSettingsOnlyThroughDeployconfig` will reject this PR's `os.Getenv` calls. #517 merges cleanly with this PR.

Code review from `/code-review high` (Claude Code), run across all four open PRs. Four findings are inline. A fifth, below, is about a file this PR doesn't change, so it can't be anchored in the diff. All five come from reading the code; none was run. CI is green.

The inline finding on `cmd/web/main.go` is a conflict with #518: whichever of the two lands second fails #518's new test.

**`bootstrap deploy-agent` still requires a cidr on every network**

https://github.com/ehharvey/homelab-ops/blob/ae7dd448fa5e51196da7ba94aef2d031f310be63/cmd/bootstrap/cmd/deploy_agent.go#L75

This PR makes names-only (state-addressed) networks legal in synced fleets, and the agent's Clone now uses `ValidateUnresolved`. But `bootstrap deploy-agent` still runs `config.Validate` on the same config-repo files, and `Validate` requires a cidr.

Scenario: a public-repo operator (the shipped `CONFIG_REPO_PRIVATE` default) has a `networks.yaml` holding only `name: lan`, and runs `bootstrap deploy-agent --file networks.yaml --file instances.yaml --file apps.yaml`. It fails with `networks[0].cidr: must be a valid CIDR`. So the break-glass bring-up path (§27) can't be used for the very fleets this PR enables, even though deploying the agent never reads addressing. It probably wants the same `ValidateUnresolved` the agent's Clone uses.

Addressed in 2e804ef:

**`bootstrap deploy-agent` still requires a cidr** (code review): taken. `deploy-agent` now validates with `config.ValidateUnresolved`, as the agent's own sync does. It reads the same config-repo files and never reads addressing, so a public repo's name-only Network deploys. It still rejects partial addressing and a `static_ip` on a state-addressed network. Test: `TestDeployAgentAcceptsNameOnlyNetwork`. Config Schema now says `render-seed` alone keeps requiring full Networks.

**§28's "all of the addressing fields" → "a `cidr`"** (`/review-work` gap): the operator signed off on the "a `cidr`" reading in this session. The §28 History line now cites the operator's #199 answers and §29 for the first two choices, and for this one, the operator's sign-off on PR #516 with the real reason: `gateway`, `dhcp_excluded_range` and `dns` were always optional in `config.Validate`, so a strict reading would reject fleets that validate today. The Plan's "several have no `dns` or no range" claim is reworded too. The shipped examples and the dev fixture all set all four fields, so it was wrong as stated.

**Landing order with #518:** unchanged. See the reply on the `cmd/web/main.go` thread.
